title: Isolating cervico-vaginal fluid cells from Macaca mulatta during pregnancy
author: Short, Cappelletti, et al.

steps.title: Set up biosafety cabinet and equipment
steps.instruction: Treat all Macaca samples as potentially Herpes B virus–positive and E. coli–exposed; work in a class II BSL‑2 cabinet, decontaminate it with UV light, place a container with 10 % (v/v) bleach solution for liquid waste, add absorbent pads, tube racks and pre‑labeled cryotubes, pre‑label two FACS tubes (unstained and full stained) and one sterile 15 mL tube with the animal ID and collection date, pre‑chill the centrifuge and microcentrifuge to 4 °C for 15 min, and fill a bucket with enough wet ice to keep samples chilled.

substeps.instruction: Consider Macaca samples potentially infected with Herpes B and E. coli; use a class II BSL‑2 cabinet.
Decontaminate the cabinet with UV light.
Place a container with 10 % (v/v) bleach solution for liquid waste inside the cabinet.
Add absorbent pads, tube racks, and pre‑labeled cryotubes.
Pre‑label two FACS tubes for each sample/time point (unstained and full stained).
Pre‑label one sterile 15 mL tube with animal ID and CVL collection date.
Pre‑chill the centrifuge to 4 °C for 15 min before sample collection.
Pre‑chill the microcentrifuge to 4 °C for 15 min before sample collection.
Fill a bucket with sufficient wet ice to keep tubes and samples chilled.

steps.title: Record CVL volume and vortex sample
steps.instruction: Measure and record the volume of the collected cervico‑vaginal lavage (CVL) and vortex the conical tube to ensure no cell pellet remains at the bottom.

steps.title: Determine CVL clarity and perform trypan blue dilution
steps.instruction: If the CVL appears clear, dilute 1:1 with trypan blue; if cloudy, dilute 1:5 with trypan blue, resuspend, load 10 µL into a disposable hemocytometer, and perform the cell count.

substeps.instruction: Dilute clear CVL 1:1 with trypan blue.
Dilute cloudy CVL 1:5 with trypan blue.
Resuspend the CVL/trypan blue mixture.
Load 10 µL into a disposable hemocytometer.
Count cells and assess viability.

steps.title: Record cell count and adjust concentration
steps.instruction: Record the cell count and viability (typically >99 %); then adjust the suspension to 1 × 10⁶ cells per 250 µL using 1X PBS, aiming for 0.5 × 10⁶ cells in 125 µL for slide loading.

steps.title: Label microscope slides and mounting assembly
steps.instruction: Label two microscope slides for each sample/time point, then assemble the Cytoclip holder in the order: stainless‑steel Cytoclip, pre‑labeled slide, filter card, disposable Cytofunnel sample chamber.

steps.title: Cytospin cells onto slides
steps.instruction: Place the assembled chambers in the Cytospin, dispense 125 µL (containing 0.5 × 10⁶ cells) into each chamber, spin for 5 min at 1600 rpm, carefully remove the slides, and let them dry for 10 min at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Place chambers in Cytospin.
Dispense 125 µL per chamber.
Spin 5 min at 1600 rpm.
Remove slides and dry 10 min at RT.

steps.title: Stain slides and dry
steps.instruction: Stain the dried slides with the Differential Quick Stain Kit, then let them dry for 15 min at room temperature before microscopic examination of cell composition.

substeps.instruction: Apply Differential Quick Stain Kit to slides.
Dry slides 15 min at RT.
Examine slides under a microscope.

steps.title: Prepare antibody mix for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Prepare the antibody cocktail as listed in the key resources table, keep it at 4 °C and protected from light by foil.

steps.title: Label FACS tubes for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Pre‑label two 5 mL polystyrene round‑bottom FACS tubes (one ‘unstained’, one ‘full stained’) for each sample.

steps.title: Resuspend cell pellet and filter
steps.instruction: After collecting the supernatant, resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL PBS, add this suspension to a 5 mL round‑bottom tube with a cell‑strainer cap to remove aggregates, replace the cap with a new one, then spin 4 min at 930 × g at 4 °C and discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 1 mL PBS.
Transfer to tube with cell‑strainer cap.
Replace cap with a new one.
Spin 4 min at 930 × g, 4 °C.
Discard supernatant carefully.

steps.title: Count cells and second wash
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in 1 mL PBS, count them as described earlier, spin again 4 min at 930 × g at 4 °C, and discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend in 1 mL PBS.
Count cells (see step 23 protocol).
Spin 4 min at 930 × g, 4 °C.
Discard supernatant carefully.

steps.title: Block cells and aliquot for staining
steps.instruction: Resuspend 0.5–1 × 10⁶ cells in 50 µL blocking buffer, dispense 50 µL into each pre‑labeled tube (unstained and full stained), and incubate 10 min at 4 °C protected from light.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend 0.5–1 × 10⁶ cells in 50 µL blocking buffer.
Add 50 µL to each pre‑labeled tube.
Incubate 10 min at 4 °C in foil.

steps.title: Add antibodies and incubate
steps.instruction: Add the antibody cocktail to the ‘full stained’ tube and 50 µL FACS buffer to the ‘unstained’ tube, cover both with foil, and incubate 20 min at 4 °C protected from light.

steps.title: Wash cells twice
steps.instruction: To each tube, add 500 µL cold FACS washing buffer, spin 4 min at 930 × g at 4 °C, carefully aspirate the supernatant, then repeat the wash (add buffer, spin, aspirate).

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL cold FACS washing buffer.
Spin 4 min at 930 × g, 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant without disturbing pellet.
Repeat wash step.

steps.title: Resuspend final cells for acquisition
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final cell pellet in 200 µL BD stabilizing solution; acquire at least 500 000 live events per tube on the flow cytometer.
